title: Microsoft Information Protection and Compliance Administrator (SC-400)

nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: Your organisation wants every Word, Excel and PowerPoint document that contains at least 10 EU passport numbers to be automatically classified as 'Highly Confidential' and encrypted so only members of the Legal group can open it. Users must NOT be prompted to accept the label — the classification must apply invisibly at ingestion in SharePoint Online and OneDrive. Which Microsoft Purview capability do you configure?
flashcards.back: Service-side auto-labelling policies inspect content at rest in SharePoint Online, OneDrive and Exchange and apply sensitivity labels — including encryption and scoped user/group access — without any user interaction, which is precisely the requirement. Client-side auto-labelling (Office apps) only recommends or applies on save inside the app, not on ingestion, and requires the file to be opened. DLP prevents sharing but does not classify or encrypt with a label. Retention labels govern lifecycle (keep/delete), not confidentiality or access; information barriers segregate communication, not file access on a label basis.

flashcards.front: A DLP policy must prevent users from copying files containing credit-card numbers to USB drives on managed Windows 10/11 endpoints, while still allowing writes to an approved encrypted USB vendor. What must you configure for this to work?
flashcards.back: Endpoint DLP requires devices to be onboarded to Microsoft Purview (via Intune, GPO or script), then a DLP policy scoped to the Devices location can block 'Copy to a USB removable device' when the file matches a sensitive-info type — with a printer/USB vendor allow-list to permit the approved device by device ID/vendor ID. Conditional Access controls sign-in, not local file operations on already-open sessions. Retention labels govern lifecycle, not egress. Insider Risk Management detects risk patterns but does not enforce real-time blocking of USB writes.

flashcards.front: Legal requires financial reports to be retained for exactly 7 years starting from the report's fiscal-year-end date (not from creation), with deletion at the end. During the 7 years the file must be immutable. Which combination in Microsoft Purview meets ALL requirements?
flashcards.back: A retention label marked as a *regulatory record* is immutable (no one — including admins — can remove the label or change its retention behaviour), and the retention period can be started by an event (e.g. 'Fiscal year end') and deleted at end. A retention policy without event-based triggers starts from creation/modified and cannot pin the start to a business event; Preservation Lock addresses reversibility of the policy but not per-item event start. Sensitivity labels handle confidentiality/access, not lifecycle immutability. Custom flows are neither immutable nor supported as a compliance control.

flashcards.front: You want alerts when a departing employee — flagged by HR (Workday) as having submitted a resignation — starts downloading unusually large volumes of files from SharePoint in the 30 days before their leave date. What do you configure in Microsoft Purview?
flashcards.back: IRM's 'Data theft by departing users' template ingests HR events via the Microsoft 365 HR connector (Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, custom CSV, etc.) to define the risk window around a resignation/termination date and correlates it with exfiltration signals (downloads, copies, prints, cloud uploads). DLP scoped by volume alone can't focus on departing users. Communication Compliance inspects communications, not file activity. A saved audit query is reactive/manual and lacks the risk-scoring, window logic and case management IRM provides.

Users must NOT be prompted to accept the label — the classification must apply invisibly at ingestion in SharePoint Online and OneDrive. Which Microsoft Purview capability do you configure?
choices: A sensitivity label with an auto-labelling policy (service side) that triggers on the EU passport number SIT with a minimum count of 10 and applies encryption scoped to the Legal group
A sensitivity label with a client-side auto-labelling policy pushed to Word/Excel/PowerPoint via the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center
A DLP policy that detects EU passport numbers and blocks external sharing, combined with a manual label applied by content owners
A retention label with an event-based trigger that fires when the document is uploaded and a Purview information barrier restricting Legal-group access

DLP prevents sharing but does not classify or encrypt with a label. Retention labels govern lifecycle (keep/delete), not confidentiality or access; information barriers segregate communication, not file access on a label basis.

questions.q: A DLP policy must prevent users from copying files containing credit-card numbers to USB drives on managed Windows 10/11 endpoints, while still allowing writes to an approved encrypted USB vendor. What must you configure for this to work?
choices: Enable device onboarding to Microsoft Purview, author a DLP policy with the Devices location scoped to the credit-card SIT, block 'Copy to a USB removable device', and add the approved vendor to the unallowed USB device exclusions list
Deploy a conditional access policy that requires a compliant device and blocks writes to removable media, then classify files with a 'CreditCard' sensitivity label
Publish a retention label with a 'Do not copy externally' setting and enable endpoint audit logging so violations are caught after the fact
Create an Insider Risk Management policy with the 'Data theft by departing users' template and quarantine the endpoint on the first exfiltration signal

choices: A retention label configured as a regulatory record, with retention triggered by an event and disposition set to delete at the end
A retention policy applied to the SharePoint site with a 7-year period from last-modified date and a Preservation Lock
A sensitivity label with an encryption right that revokes access after 7 years
A data lifecycle policy that runs a Power Automate flow to move files to an immutable Blob container after each fiscal year

questions.q: You want alerts when a departing employee — flagged by HR (Workday) as having submitted a resignation — starts downloading unusually large volumes of files from SharePoint in the 30 days before their leave date. What do you configure in Microsoft Purview?
choices: An Insider Risk Management policy from the 'Data theft by departing users' template, with the HR connector configured to import resignation events
A DLP policy scoped to SharePoint with an incident report sent to the employee's manager on any download above 500 MB
A Communication Compliance policy scanning outbound email for the phrase 'my last day'
An audit search saved query filtered to SharePoint FileDownloaded activity for the Departing-Users group

nodes.title: AWS analytics services: Key Ideas
nodes.content: AWS offers a suite of managed analytics services covering data warehousing, stream processing, interactive querying, and BI. The Cloud Practitioner exam tests which service to use for each scenario.

flashcards.back: Columnar data warehouse for petabyte-scale SQL analytics on structured data; not for OLTP or real-time streaming.

flashcards.front: Amazon Kinesis vs SQS — when to choose Kinesis?
flashcards.back: Kinesis for real-time ordered streaming with multiple consumers and replay; SQS for decoupled task queues with at-least-once delivery.

flashcards.front: Amazon Athena — how does it query data?
flashcards.back: Serverless interactive SQL on data stored in S3; no infrastructure to manage, pay per query (per TB scanned).

flashcards.front: AWS Glue role in an analytics pipeline?
flashcards.back: Managed ETL service: crawls data sources to build a Data Catalog, then runs serverless Spark jobs to transform and load data.

questions.q: A regulated bank must review outbound Microsoft Teams chat and Exchange Online mail for potential market manipulation phrases (a supervised sample, not 100%). Reviewers must be able to escalate, tag, and mark items for further review — and reports must be retained for the regulator. Which Purview solution do you configure?
choices: A Communication Compliance policy using a supervised sample percentage, a custom keyword classifier for market-manipulation phrases, and a defined reviewer group
A DLP policy that quarantines messages containing the classifier and forwards them to a supervisor mailbox
An eDiscovery (Premium) case with a continuous hold on the trader mailboxes and daily review of the collection
An Insider Risk Management policy using the 'Risky browser usage' template scoped to the trader group
questions.explanation: Communication Compliance is the supervisory review workflow: it samples Teams messages, Exchange email, Yammer/Viva Engage and 3rd-party ingested channels against classifiers or keyword lists, assigns reviewers, exposes escalation/tagging/mark-for-review actions and preserves an auditable trail. DLP blocks/monitors but does not provide supervised sample workflows. eDiscovery is investigative, not a supervisory review programme. Insider Risk tracks user risk, not communication-content review.

questions.q: During an eDiscovery (Premium) case you must collect from a custodian's mailbox, OneDrive, Teams chats AND their Yammer/Viva Engage community messages, then run near-duplicate detection and email threading on the review set before producing to outside counsel. Which sequence of steps supports ALL of that?
choices: Add the custodian → apply a hold → run a collection with the appropriate locations → commit the collection to a review set → run analytics (near-dupes + threading) → tag/produce from the review set
Run a Content Search across all custodian sources → export directly to a PST → hand the PST to outside counsel
Place the mailbox on Litigation Hold → export the mailbox via the Compliance Center download tool → forward Teams and Yammer messages by email
Create a Core eDiscovery case → search each location individually → export each result set separately without analytics
questions.explanation: eDiscovery (Premium) is the only tier that supports custodial holds across mailbox + OneDrive + Teams + Viva Engage together, review-set analytics (near-duplicate detection, email threading, themes, predictive coding), and structured productions. Content Search / Core eDiscovery do not include review-set analytics. Litigation Hold is mailbox-only and precludes analytics. Forwarding Teams/Yammer content by email loses provenance and defensibility.

questions.q: You need a durable, tamper-evident audit trail of high-value activities — mailbox items being read by a delegate, sensitivity-label changes on files, Exchange admin actions — retained for one year for Microsoft 365 E5 users. What must you enable and configure?
choices: Confirm the tenant is licensed for Purview Audit (Premium), then create an audit retention policy in Microsoft Purview setting the RecordType(s) to a 1-year retention
Enable Unified Audit Log ingestion and rely on the default 90-day retention, exporting nightly to a SIEM for the remaining 9 months
Configure a Log Analytics diagnostic setting on Entra ID and forward audit records via Sentinel
Use Microsoft Defender for Cloud Apps activity policies with an alert for each high-value action
questions.explanation: Purview Audit (Premium) — included with E5 — unlocks higher-value events (MailItemsAccessed, Send, SearchQueryInitiatedExchange/SharePoint), and lets you define audit retention policies up to 1 year (or 10 with the add-on). The default Unified Audit Log retention for Standard is 180 days (E3) — the reliable, in-service compliance path is to configure audit retention policies, not to export nightly. Log Analytics is for Entra logs, not the M365 Purview Audit corpus. Defender for Cloud Apps is a CASB, not the audit-of-record system.

questions.q: A sensitivity label must be applied to Teams meetings and their chats so that shared documents inherit the label and Teams recordings are encrypted. You publish the label to the users but the option to apply it on a Team, group or site is greyed out in the Purview portal. What must you do to enable that option?
choices: Enable sensitivity labels for containers by running the Microsoft Graph / PowerShell command to enable labels for Microsoft 365 Groups (EnableMIPLabels + Execute-AzureAdLabelSync), then edit the label to include 'Groups & sites' and 'Teams meetings' as scopes
Convert the sensitivity label to a retention label so that containers are supported
Set the tenant's default sharing setting to 'Anyone with the link' and re-publish the label
Enable Microsoft 365 Multi-Geo for the tenant so Team locations become taggable
questions.explanation: Sensitivity-label support for containers (Microsoft 365 Groups, Teams, SharePoint sites, Teams meetings) requires the tenant-level preview flag to be enabled via PowerShell / Graph — after which 'Groups & sites' and 'Teams meetings' appear as label scopes. Retention labels don't apply confidentiality or encryption. Sharing defaults don't gate container labelling. Multi-Geo is a data residency feature unrelated to label scopes.

nodes.title: Troubleshooting methodology: Key Ideas
nodes.content: A structured troubleshooting process beats random guessing every time. The classic flow: identify the problem precisely, form a theory, test it, fix, verify, document. Most exams test that you know the flow AND can spot the layer at which the symptom originates.

flashcards.back: CompTIA's 6-step: (1) Identify the problem (gather symptoms, questions to user, recent changes). (2) Establish a theory of probable cause. (3) Test the theory. (4) Plan and implement the fix. (5) Verify full system functionality, apply preventive measures. (6) Document everything.

flashcards.front: Top-down vs bottom-up troubleshooting on a network problem.
flashcards.back: Top-down: start at the application layer and work down — does the browser work? DNS? TCP? Routing? Bottom-up: start at the physical layer — is the cable plugged in? Link light? IP? When you suspect physical/cable, bottom-up is faster. When the user has 'a website is broken', top-down is faster.

Almost every production incident traces back to a recent change — a deploy, a config push, a vendor patch, a cert rotation. 'It was working yesterday' tells you to check today's change-log before forming an exotic theory. Recent changes are the highest-priors of the bug space.

Bisect the path between symptom and cause. If 10 hops between client and server, test hop 5. Good → problem is past hop 5. Bad → problem is before. Two more bisections narrow it to one hop. Faster than checking every link sequentially when the chain is long.

questions.q: Regulatory rules forbid investment bankers and equity-research analysts in your firm from communicating with each other in Microsoft Teams or Exchange. Which Purview feature enforces this?
choices: Information barriers, defined with two segments (Bankers, Analysts) and a blocking policy between them
A supervised Communication Compliance policy that flags all cross-department messages for reviewer
A DLP policy that blocks Teams chats between the two Entra groups
Conditional Access policies that block Teams desktop client sign-in for the two groups when the other group is signed in
questions.explanation: Information barriers create *segments* (from directory attributes such as department) and *policies* that Block/Allow communication between segments across Teams (chats, calls, meetings), OneDrive and SharePoint. Communication Compliance detects after the fact but doesn't prevent communication. DLP is content-aware, not identity-pair-aware for chat suppression. Conditional Access controls sign-in per user/session, not who can talk to whom.

questions.q: Your DLP policy correctly detects Australian tax file numbers (TFN) but is generating too many false positives on internal HR documents that legitimately reference TFNs. You must NOT weaken the rule for external sharing — only relax it for internal-only sharing by the HR department. What is the best approach?
choices: Create separate DLP rules within the same policy: one restrictive rule for external recipients keeping the current match count, and a second higher-confidence / higher-count rule scoped to internal HR sharing (with the HR group as an exception on the strict rule)
Increase the SIT match count globally to 10 so HR files stop triggering
Delete the DLP policy on the HR SharePoint site and rely on retention labels instead
Add every HR user to a 'Bypass DLP' distribution list applied at the tenant level
questions.explanation: DLP policies allow multiple rules with different conditions, exceptions and actions inside one policy. The cleanest fix is a strict external-sharing rule preserving current sensitivity and a separate, higher-threshold or higher-confidence internal rule (or an HR-group exception on the strict rule) — precisely targeting the noisy population without weakening external enforcement. Raising the global count would relax external protection too. Deleting DLP on the HR site removes the safety net. There is no supported tenant-wide 'Bypass DLP' distribution list.

questions.q: Marketing wants to freely email presentations to external partners, but Engineering documents labelled 'Confidential – Internal' must NEVER leave the tenant. Which control is the most appropriate to enforce the block?
choices: A DLP policy scoped to Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams that blocks the sending/sharing of content carrying the 'Confidential – Internal' sensitivity label to external recipients
Configure external sharing on every SharePoint site to 'Only people in your organization' — including Marketing's
A retention policy that prevents deletion for 3 years on all Engineering files, which stops external sharing until retention expires
An Insider Risk Management policy scoped to Engineering that alerts when a labelled file leaves the tenant
questions.explanation: DLP conditions can trigger on 'Content is labelled with' a sensitivity label and block external sharing/mailing across Exchange, SharePoint, OneDrive and Teams — the enforcement is real-time and does not affect Marketing's ability to share unlabelled content. Locking SharePoint tenant-wide would break Marketing's need. Retention prevents deletion, not egress. IRM is detective, not preventative.

questions.q: You publish a new sensitivity label but users in a specific country subsidiary report the label doesn't appear in their Office apps. Publishing scope in the label policy is set to 'All users and groups', and licensing has been verified. What is the most likely cause and fix?
choices: Sensitivity label policies apply based on the policy's user/group assignment and can be filtered by administrative units — verify that no more-specific competing policy with higher priority is targeting the affected users and that the label is included in the policy scope order
Sensitivity labels only replicate hourly; wait 24 hours before troubleshooting further
The Microsoft 365 Apps channel must be switched to Semi-Annual Enterprise Channel for labels to render
Rebuild the labels in a different geography's compliance portal, since labels are region-locked
questions.explanation: When multiple label policies are assigned to overlapping populations, the higher-priority policy wins for a user, and only labels included in *that* policy appear. Checking policy priority order and ensuring the intended label is included in the policy that wins for the affected users is the standard root-cause. Labels do propagate faster than 24h (the built-in latency is usually <1h for Office apps). Channel doesn't gate label visibility. Purview compliance portal is a single global tenant resource — not region-locked.
